descVi: Diễn tả trạng thái cảm xúc, thái độ, động lực và giao tiếp tinh tế.

words.definitionEn: feeling fear or worry about something
words.exampleDailyEn: The puppy was afraid of the noisy vacuum cleaner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some employees are afraid to report workplace problems because they worry about losing their jobs.

words.definitionEn: feeling strong displeasure about something unfair, wrong, or unpleasant
words.exampleDailyEn: He felt angry when someone damaged his bicycle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents became angry about the council's decision to close the only library in their neighbourhood.

words.definitionEn: Not interesting or exciting.
words.exampleDailyEn: The film was so boring that I fell asleep.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students may find repetitive exercises boring unless teachers explain their purpose and introduce variety.

words.definitionEn: Produce tears because of sadness, pain, or strong emotion.
words.exampleDailyEn: The baby began to cry when her toy fell.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Young children may cry when separated from their parents, so schools should provide a welcoming environment.

words.definitionEn: loved or valued very much
words.exampleDailyEn: This little garden is very dear to my grandmother.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Places that are dear to local residents deserve consideration when urban redevelopment plans are prepared.

words.definitionEn: Feeling very happy and enthusiastic about something.
words.exampleDailyEn: The children were excited about their first camping trip.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students are often more excited about learning when lessons involve practical experiments and opportunities for discovery.

words.definitionEn: Making someone feel eager, enthusiastic, or thrilled.
words.exampleDailyEn: The final minutes of the match were incredibly exciting.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Advances in renewable energy offer exciting opportunities for young engineers seeking to address global environmental challenges.

words.definitionEn: Experience an emotion, physical sensation, or personal belief.
words.exampleDailyEn: I feel much warmer with this soft blanket.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents often feel safer when public spaces are well lit and regularly maintained by local authorities.

words.definitionEn: An emotional state or response to something
words.exampleDailyEn: A feeling of relief washed over me after the exam.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A strong feeling of belonging can improve students' confidence and encourage participation in school activities.

words.definitionEn: making you laugh or smile
words.exampleDailyEn: That funny story made everyone at the table laugh.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers sometimes use funny examples to make difficult concepts more memorable and encourage students to participate.

words.definitionEn: To dislike someone or something very strongly.
words.exampleDailyEn: I hate finding wet socks on the bathroom floor.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although many commuters hate crowded trains, affordable public transport remains essential for reducing urban traffic.

words.definitionEn: Wanting to learn about or take part in something.
words.exampleDailyEn: My sister is interested in learning to grow vegetables.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students who are interested in science should have regular opportunities to conduct practical experiments.

words.definitionEn: To make sounds showing amusement or happiness.
words.exampleDailyEn: The baby's funny dance made everyone laugh at dinner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: People who laugh together regularly may develop stronger social bonds and cope better with everyday stress.

words.definitionEn: feel deep affection for someone or enjoy something very much
words.exampleDailyEn: I love walking by the river after dinner.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can develop children's love of reading by providing diverse books and regular library visits.

words.definitionEn: Having good things happen by chance.
words.exampleDailyEn: We were lucky to catch the last bus home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although some entrepreneurs benefit from lucky opportunities, long-term business success usually requires careful planning and consistent effort.

words.definitionEn: To raise the corners of your mouth, showing happiness or friendliness.
words.exampleDailyEn: The baby smiled when I waved across the room.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A friendly smile can help patients feel more comfortable when discussing their concerns with healthcare professionals.

words.definitionEn: feeling regret about something you did or something that happened
words.exampleDailyEn: I'm sorry I spilled juice on your clean shirt.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although companies may say they are sorry for environmental damage, meaningful action is needed to restore public trust.

words.definitionEn: Extremely good or enjoyable.
words.exampleDailyEn: We had a wonderful picnic beside the lake.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public libraries offer wonderful opportunities for children to discover new interests without placing financial pressure on families.

words.definitionEn: Causing great surprise or admiration.
words.exampleDailyEn: The view from the mountain was absolutely amazing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Recent medical research has produced amazing results, offering new hope to patients with previously untreatable conditions.

words.definitionEn: very unreasonable, foolish, or strange
words.exampleDailyEn: It seems crazy to wear sandals in this snow.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although some people consider car-free cities a crazy idea, such policies could significantly improve urban air quality.

words.definitionEn: extremely good or enjoyable
words.exampleDailyEn: We had a fantastic view of the mountains from our balcony.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Community sports programmes offer young people a fantastic opportunity to develop teamwork skills and build confidence.

words.definitionEn: An unpleasant feeling about danger or something bad happening.
words.exampleDailyEn: She held my hand because of her fear of heights.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Fear of failure may prevent students from asking questions, especially in highly competitive learning environments.

words.definitionEn: Feeling happy or pleased about something.
words.exampleDailyEn: I'm glad you came to dinner with us tonight.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many residents were glad that the council had decided to preserve the local park.

words.definitionEn: The feeling of being pleased or satisfied with life.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her face shone with happiness when the puppy arrived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Strong social connections often contribute more to lasting happiness than the purchase of expensive possessions.

words.definitionEn: to want something to happen and believe it may happen
words.exampleDailyEn: I hope the rain stops before our picnic.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many graduates hope to find meaningful employment that allows them to contribute positively to society.

words.definitionEn: Unhappy because you lack companionship or close connections.
words.exampleDailyEn: I felt lonely until my neighbour invited me for tea.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Older adults may feel lonely after retirement, so community centres should provide regular opportunities for social interaction.

words.definitionEn: Feeling pleased about achievements or people you care about.
words.exampleDailyEn: He felt proud of the cake he baked himself.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents are often proud of their cultural heritage and support efforts to preserve historic buildings.

words.definitionEn: Feeling afraid of something or worried that something bad might happen.
words.exampleDailyEn: The puppy looked scared when it heard the thunder.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students who are scared of making mistakes may avoid speaking during foreign language lessons.

words.definitionEn: Making someone feel afraid or nervous.
words.exampleDailyEn: That scary noise was just a branch against the window.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Starting school can be scary for young children, so teachers should create a welcoming environment.

words.definitionEn: An unexpected event, or the feeling it causes.
words.exampleDailyEn: Finding a birthday cake in the kitchen was a lovely surprise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The survey results may surprise policymakers who assume that young people prefer online learning.

words.definitionEn: Feeling that something unexpected has happened.
words.exampleDailyEn: I was surprised to find flowers outside my door.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Researchers were surprised by how strongly access to green spaces influenced residents' reported levels of wellbeing.

words.definitionEn: unexpected and causing a feeling of surprise
words.exampleDailyEn: The tiny bakery offers a surprising variety of fresh bread.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The survey revealed a surprising decline in car ownership among young adults living in major cities.

words.definitionEn: To want something, especially something unlikely or not currently true.
words.exampleDailyEn: I wish our flat had a bigger kitchen.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many residents wish their neighbourhoods had more green spaces where children could play safely and families could relax.

words.definitionEn: feeling anxious about problems or something that might happen
words.exampleDailyEn: She looked worried when her cat failed to return.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many parents are worried about the effects of excessive screen time on their children's sleep.

words.definitionEn: To feel anxious, or make someone feel anxious.
words.exampleDailyEn: I worry about my cat when she stays outside.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many parents worry that excessive screen time may affect their children's sleep and concentration.

words.definitionEn: To respect someone for their qualities or achievements
words.exampleDailyEn: I admire my sister for staying calm under pressure.
words.exampleIeltsEn: People often admire successful athletes for their determination, but consistent training is equally important.

words.definitionEn: To make someone feel slightly angry or irritated.
words.exampleDailyEn: Those dripping taps annoy me when I try to sleep.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Frequent online advertisements can annoy users and discourage them from returning to otherwise useful educational websites.

words.definitionEn: shout happily to show approval or encouragement
words.exampleDailyEn: We cheered as our neighbour crossed the finish line.
words.exampleIeltsEn: When spectators cheer for every participant, community sporting events can foster a stronger sense of belonging.

words.definitionEn: A pleasant state of physical ease and relaxation.
words.exampleDailyEn: I enjoyed the comfort of a warm bed after camping.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Support groups can comfort patients by providing opportunities to share experiences and discuss concerns openly.

words.definitionEn: Belief in your abilities or in a successful outcome.
words.exampleDailyEn: Practising with friends gave me confidence before the interview.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Supportive feedback can build students' confidence and encourage them to participate more actively in classroom discussions.

words.definitionEn: Tell someone you are pleased about their success or good fortune.
words.exampleDailyEn: We called to congratulate Lina on her new job.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should congratulate students on personal improvement rather than focus exclusively on high examination scores.

words.definitionEn: Ability to face danger or difficulty despite feeling afraid.
words.exampleDailyEn: It took courage to admit my mistake in class.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Young people need courage to challenge unfair practices, especially when their opinions differ from those of others.
collocations: have the courage to do something

words.definitionEn: to have enough courage to do something
words.exampleDailyEn: I finally dared to sing in front of everyone.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students are more likely to dare to question established ideas when teachers welcome respectful disagreement.

words.definitionEn: To make someone unhappy by failing to meet their expectations.
words.exampleDailyEn: I knew cancelling our picnic would disappoint the children.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public transport improvements may disappoint commuters if services remain unreliable despite substantial investment in new vehicles.

words.definitionEn: sadness because something was not as good as expected
words.exampleDailyEn: Her face showed disappointment when the picnic was cancelled.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teaching young people to cope with disappointment can help them respond more positively to academic setbacks.

words.definitionEn: To find someone or something unpleasant or not enjoyable.
words.exampleDailyEn: I dislike waiting outside when it is raining.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Some students dislike group assignments because they feel that individual contributions are not assessed fairly.

words.definitionEn: a feeling of great enthusiasm and eager anticipation
words.exampleDailyEn: The children jumped with excitement when the puppies arrived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although international sporting events generate excitement, host cities must carefully assess their long-term financial costs.

words.definitionEn: Stop blaming someone or feeling angry about what they did.
words.exampleDailyEn: Can you forgive me for breaking your favourite mug?
words.exampleIeltsEn: International lenders may forgive some debts to help poorer countries invest more in healthcare and education.

words.definitionEn: To make someone feel afraid.
words.exampleDailyEn: Sudden loud noises can frighten our new puppy.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Alarming news reports may frighten children, so adults should explain difficult events in an appropriate way.

words.definitionEn: a strong feeling of fear, shock, or disgust
words.exampleDailyEn: She watched in horror as her laptop fell downstairs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Horror films often use music and lighting to create tension rather than relying entirely on frightening images.

words.definitionEn: The quality of being funny or the ability to appreciate funniness.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her gentle humour made everyone at dinner feel relaxed.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers can use humour to reduce classroom anxiety and encourage students to participate more confidently.

words.definitionEn: An insulting word for someone considered very foolish.
words.exampleDailyEn: I felt like an idiot after losing my keys again.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Calling a classmate an idiot can damage their confidence and undermine efforts to create a supportive learning environment.

words.definitionEn: A feeling of great happiness
words.exampleDailyEn: The children jumped for joy when the snow began.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Community gardens can bring joy to residents while strengthening social connections and encouraging healthier lifestyles.

words.definitionEn: The sound or action of laughing
words.exampleDailyEn: Laughter filled the kitchen when the puppy sneezed.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Shared laughter can strengthen social bonds and help people manage stress in demanding work environments.

words.definitionEn: the way someone feels at a particular time
words.exampleDailyEn: A short walk usually puts me in a better mood.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Access to green spaces can improve residents' mood and encourage more positive interactions within urban communities.

words.definitionEn: a frightening or deeply unpleasant dream
words.exampleDailyEn: I woke from a nightmare and switched on the lamp.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Without reliable public transport, commuting can become a nightmare for people living outside major cities.

words.definitionEn: a very strong enthusiasm for an activity or subject
words.exampleDailyEn: Her passion for baking fills our kitchen with delicious smells.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers who share their passion for science can inspire students to pursue careers in research.

words.definitionEn: Sadness and concern for someone who is suffering.
words.exampleDailyEn: I felt pity for the puppy shivering in the rain.
words.exampleIeltsEn: It is a pity that many historic buildings are demolished before their cultural value is properly assessed.

words.definitionEn: A feeling of happiness or enjoyment
words.exampleDailyEn: She takes great pleasure in growing herbs on her balcony.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public libraries encourage reading for pleasure while providing affordable access to knowledge for people of all ages.

words.definitionEn: Pleasure and satisfaction in achievements, qualities, or people you value.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her face shone with pride as she displayed her painting.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools can foster community pride by encouraging students to participate in projects that improve their local environment.

words.definitionEn: to feel sorry about something that happened or was done
words.exampleDailyEn: I regret leaving my umbrella at home this morning.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Graduates may regret choosing a career solely for its salary if the work provides little personal satisfaction.

words.definitionEn: a loving relationship or the excitement and affection surrounding love
words.exampleDailyEn: Their romance began during a walking holiday in the mountains.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Popular films often portray romance in idealised ways, which may shape young people's expectations of relationships.

words.definitionEn: to make someone feel frightened
words.exampleDailyEn: Please knock gently so you don't scare the baby.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Misleading reports about food safety can scare consumers and damage public confidence in local producers.

words.definitionEn: To give a loud, high cry from strong emotion.
words.exampleDailyEn: The children screamed with excitement as the ride began.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Residents complain that visitors scream late at night, disturbing sleep and reducing the neighbourhood's quality of life.

words.definitionEn: A painful feeling caused by doing something wrong or embarrassing.
words.exampleDailyEn: He felt shame after lying to his closest friend.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should address bullying without creating a culture of shame that prevents pupils from seeking help.

words.definitionEn: a strong feeling of surprise caused by something unexpected
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden rise in rent came as a shock.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Moving abroad can cause culture shock, particularly when everyday customs differ greatly from those at home.

words.definitionEn: A warm feeling of love or fondness for someone or something.
words.exampleDailyEn: Our cat shows affection by rubbing against our legs.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Children who receive consistent affection from caregivers often develop greater emotional security and stronger social relationships.

words.definitionEn: a strong feeling of displeasure about something wrong or unfair
words.exampleDailyEn: He took a deep breath to control his anger.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public anger over rising transport costs can encourage local authorities to reconsider their pricing policies.

words.definitionEn: Worry or nervousness about something uncertain or threatening.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her anxiety faded when she heard the good news.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Regular physical activity can reduce anxiety among students facing demanding examinations and uncertain career prospects.

words.definitionEn: A feeling of gratitude for someone's help or kindness.
words.exampleDailyEn: We baked our neighbour a cake to show our appreciation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Arts education can develop students' appreciation of cultural traditions that differ from their own.

words.definitionEn: a feeling of great pleasure or happiness
words.exampleDailyEn: The children squealed with delight when the puppy arrived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Public gardens can bring delight to city residents while providing valuable spaces for relaxation and social interaction.

words.definitionEn: the firm intention to continue despite difficulties
words.exampleDailyEn: Despite the rain, she finished the race with determination.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students who show determination are often better able to overcome academic setbacks and achieve their goals.

words.definitionEn: great emotional pain, worry, or unhappiness
words.exampleDailyEn: Her neighbour noticed her distress and offered to help.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Sudden unemployment can cause considerable distress, particularly for households with limited savings and high housing costs.

words.definitionEn: an uncomfortable feeling caused by awkwardness or fear of others' judgment
words.exampleDailyEn: I blushed with embarrassment when I forgot my neighbour's name.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Fear of embarrassment may prevent language learners from practising their speaking skills in front of others.

words.definitionEn: a strong feeling such as joy, fear, or sadness
words.exampleDailyEn: Her voice shook with emotion when she saw her brother.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teaching children to recognise and manage emotion can improve their relationships and support long-term mental health.

words.definitionEn: To suffer something difficult or unpleasant without giving up.
words.exampleDailyEn: We endured hours of noise while workers repaired the roof.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Communities in dry regions must endure prolonged water shortages as climate patterns become less predictable.

words.definitionEn: Strong interest and excitement about something you enjoy or value.
words.exampleDailyEn: The children showed real enthusiasm for planting their own vegetables.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Teachers who demonstrate enthusiasm for their subjects can motivate students to explore ideas beyond the classroom.

words.definitionEn: Annoyance caused by being unable to achieve what you want.
words.exampleDailyEn: She sighed in frustration when the printer jammed again.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Repeated delays in public transport can increase commuters' frustration and reduce their confidence in local services.

words.definitionEn: Deep sadness, especially after someone you love has died
words.exampleDailyEn: She found comfort in friends during her grief.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Schools should offer counselling to help young people manage grief after the loss of a family member.

words.definitionEn: To smile widely, usually showing your teeth.
words.exampleDailyEn: She grinned when her puppy brought back the ball.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A friendly grin from a teacher may help nervous students feel more comfortable participating in classroom discussions.

words.definitionEn: An extraordinary event that seems impossible or beyond natural explanation.
words.exampleDailyEn: It was a miracle that the vase survived.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Although new technology can appear to work miracles, lasting environmental progress also requires changes in public behaviour.

words.definitionEn: great unhappiness or suffering
words.exampleDailyEn: The constant noise made her life a misery.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Improving access to affordable housing can reduce the misery experienced by families living in overcrowded temporary accommodation.

words.definitionEn: The belief that good things will happen.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her optimism helped us stay cheerful during the storm.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Despite economic uncertainty, many graduates express optimism about their chances of finding meaningful employment.

words.definitionEn: To affect someone so strongly they cannot cope.
words.exampleDailyEn: I felt overwhelmed by everyone's kindness after the move.
words.exampleIeltsEn: A sudden increase in visitors can overwhelm local infrastructure unless tourism growth is carefully managed.

words.definitionEn: sudden strong fear that makes clear thinking difficult
words.exampleDailyEn: I felt a moment of panic when my keys disappeared.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Clear communication during emergencies can reduce public panic and help people follow safety instructions more effectively.

words.definitionEn: An extremely strong feeling of anger.
words.exampleDailyEn: He shook with rage when he discovered his broken bicycle.
words.exampleIeltsEn: As wildfires rage across dry regions, local authorities must coordinate evacuations and provide temporary accommodation.

words.definitionEn: The act of refusing to accept someone or something.
words.exampleDailyEn: After another rejection, she revised her job application.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Repeated rejection in the labour market can damage young people's confidence and discourage further job applications.

words.definitionEn: Comfort felt when worry or fear ends
words.exampleDailyEn: I sighed with relief when my missing cat returned.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Rapid delivery of emergency relief can prevent further suffering in communities affected by severe flooding.

words.definitionEn: Pleasure felt when needs, wishes, or expectations are fulfilled.
words.exampleDailyEn: He smiled with satisfaction after fixing the broken chair.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Greater job satisfaction can reduce staff turnover and encourage employees to contribute more actively to their organisations.

words.definitionEn: To breathe out slowly and audibly, expressing feelings
words.exampleDailyEn: Dad sighed when he saw the muddy floor.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Many commuters breathe a sigh of relief when reliable public transport reduces the stress of their daily journeys.

words.definitionEn: Inner strength, courage, or enthusiasm
words.exampleDailyEn: Even after losing, our team showed great spirit.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Community projects can strengthen a spirit of cooperation and encourage residents to take pride in their neighbourhoods.

words.definitionEn: A desire to upset or hurt someone deliberately.
words.exampleDailyEn: He hid his sister's favourite toy out of spite.
words.exampleIeltsEn: In spite of limited funding, the community centre continues to provide valuable support for local families.

words.definitionEn: To make someone feel extremely frightened.
words.exampleDailyEn: Sudden thunder can terrify our dog during summer storms.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Extreme weather events can terrify young children, making clear explanations and reassurance from adults especially important.

words.definitionEn: An extremely strong feeling of fear.
words.exampleDailyEn: She woke in terror after dreaming about a falling lift.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Responsible news reporting should inform the public about threats without spreading unnecessary terror among communities.

words.definitionEn: The readiness to do something without needing to be forced.
words.exampleDailyEn: Her willingness to help made the move much easier.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Students' willingness to ask questions often increases when teachers create a supportive classroom environment.

words.definitionEn: A strong feeling that someone or something deserves no respect
words.exampleDailyEn: He showed contempt for my suggestion by laughing.
words.exampleIeltsEn: When officials treat public concerns with contempt, trust in democratic institutions can decline significantly.

words.definitionEn: Intended to hurt someone through harsh criticism or unkind remarks.
words.exampleDailyEn: His cutting remark about her cooking spoiled the meal.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Cutting comments from teachers can discourage students from asking questions and participating actively in class.

words.definitionEn: to bring a feeling, memory or image into someone's mind
words.exampleDailyEn: The smell of fresh bread evokes memories of home.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Traditional music can evoke a strong sense of belonging among people living far from their homeland.

words.definitionEn: to keep returning to someone's mind and causing distress
words.exampleDailyEn: That embarrassing mistake still haunts me before every presentation.
words.exampleIeltsEn: The consequences of poor urban planning can haunt communities long after the original decisions are made.

words.definitionEn: to become stronger or make a feeling or effect stronger
words.exampleDailyEn: The sudden silence only heightened my curiosity about the surprise.
words.exampleIeltsEn: Repeated droughts may heighten public concern about water shortages and encourage governments to invest in conservation.
